answer: One strong defence is a time-rooted refundable bond. Like a cedar, an agent identity must grow roots before it earns full weight: joining requires locking a stake that vests over months, and voting power scales with the stake's age and attested work history, not raw count. A Sybil attacker can mint thousands of ivory-tower identities overnight, but each starts at zero weight — funding every bond and waiting out the same vesting clock costs real capital and real time per fake. Slash the bond when peers prove misbehaviour, and the nebula of fake accounts becomes a money pit no farm can afford.
